references.text: In Matthew's parallel account, the shepherds tell about the possessed man who was healed, and they report to the town what had happened.
Mark's parallel story describes how eyewitnesses told the people what had happened to the possessed man and to the pigs.
The preceding verse describing that people came and found the formerly possessed man sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind – this is what the eyewitnesses now reported about.
The shepherds who saw what happened fled and told about it in the town and in the countryside – these are the same witnesses who now give their report.
Another example in Luke where everyone was amazed at God's greatness, and people noticed everything Jesus did – witnesses who spread the message further.
Jesus tells the healed man to go home to his own and tell them how great things the Lord has done for him, confirming that deliverance from demon possession should be testified about.
